measured: The demand scan does not read volter-ai/videogame-ai (a private repository the scan's applications list does not hold), so its use is the sourced ruling recorded beside it in twin-world's demand/vendor-identities.json (demandedBy: owner volter, product videogame-ai, source docs/adr/0002-the-games-ecosystem-sandbox.md). Read at origin/videogame-run-2 3ad856dc1128: ADR 0002 decision 2 makes Instagram a Protocol 3 pack of the games-ecosystem sandbox, and its Consequences name a launch as a trailer posted to TikTok, Instagram and YouTube and then running the community. The calls below are what a game studio's tooling makes for that through the Instagram API with Instagram Login: connecting an account (the authorization window, the code exchange, the long-lived token and its refresh), reading the professional account, publishing a Reel and an image (container, status, publish, the publishing limit), reading its media, their fields and insights, and the community side (comments, replies, hiding and deleting). e2e/people/ at that commit holds no Instagram client yet (platforms.mjs: reddit, x, discord, tiktok); its TikTok person is the model for Instagram's audience, an account signed up on the platform whose acts on the game's media are the twin's door, as an audience is no API.

applications.name: volter-ai/videogame-ai
applications.client: a game studio's launch tooling calling the Instagram API with Instagram Login with fetch (Meta publishes no Node SDK for it), by the ruling of docs/adr/0002-the-games-ecosystem-sandbox.md
applications.gate: ADR 0002 decision 2: the sandbox World serves Instagram as a Protocol 3 twin (docs/adr/0002-the-games-ecosystem-sandbox.md:35-38).

frontend.call: Business Login for Instagram: the studio or a creator is sent to the authorization window and back with a code

backend.call: POST api.instagram.com/oauth/access_token: the code for a short-lived token, the user id and the permissions
POST /{ig-user-id}/media with media_type=REELS and video_url (the trailer), or image_url (key art): a container
GET /{container-id}?fields=status_code; GET /{media-id}?fields=...; GET, POST and DELETE on an IG Comment by its id
GET /{media-id}/insights?metric=...: the trailer's views, reach, likes, comments, saves and shares
GET and POST /{media-id}/comments: the community's comments, and the studio's own
GET and POST /{comment-id}/replies: answering a comment

standIns: the App Dashboard's app (its Instagram App ID and secret, its OAuth redirect URIs, and the long-lived token it generates for the studio's own account) is the credential door's; a person's Instagram account (signed up on instagram.com, switched to a professional account or not) is the accounts door's; the audience at work on a media (its views, reach, likes, saves and shares, and a comment by someone whose acts are no API call) is the audience door's. The twin decodes no media: a Reel's duration is read from its MP4 boxes and an image's size from its JPEG frame header.
